findings.message: The no-leak tests check only clueFor(ruin) (puzzles.test.ts 'serialise to nothing but the site's content', determinism.test.ts clueFor check). No test checks the object openRuin actually returns to the player (OpenResult: clue, lockedUntil, solved), for example that opened.result.clue equals clueFor(ruin) and that the serialised OpenResult has no answer or minMoves. operations.test.ts:184 only asserts the clue is not null, and determinism.test.ts serialises openRuin results without checking them. If a field that carries a secret were added to OpenResult, no test would fail.
findings.requirement: `openRuin` starts a player's session at the ruin and returns only the clue: what the site shows, never the answer.

findings.message: The lockout tests cover other players (operations.test.ts 'locks out a wrong answer for three seconds, for that player only') and leaving and reopening (puzzles.test.ts 'keeps a lockout when the player leaves and reopens the ruin'). No scripted test shows that a player locked out at one ruin can still answer at a different ruin during that lockout, which is the per-ruin half of the per-(player, ruin) scoping.
findings.requirement: A wrong attempt locks that player out of that ruin for 3 s.

findings.message: Only one or two specific minimum routes per puzzle are shown to be accepted: the evaluator's BFS route in W,S,E,N order (reader test) and the first valid string in shortest-first N,E,S,W order (guesser, first 40 navigation ruins). Separately, determinism.test.ts uses a BFS rightAnswer. No test enumerates every minimum-length route of a puzzle with the independent evaluator and asserts that answerRuin accepts each one. No test shows that a valid route longer than the minimum is refused as wrong. The only wrong navigation attempt in operations.test.ts is the one-move ['N'].
findings.requirement: Any path of the minimum length is accepted.

findings.message: No check exercises the dist side (types/default) of the new subpath exports. The tests import @pirate-sea-race/content/ruins through the @pirate-sea-race/source condition. The build log shows that the postbuild scripts and scripts/smoke-build.ts WORKSPACE_EXPORTS (13 entries) do not include @pirate-sea-race/simulation/ruins or @pirate-sea-race/content/ruins. Only the worker's own hand-run node load, reported in its summary, supports them. The fix is in root/postbuild files outside the lane's owned paths, so it belongs to the integrator or a later feature.
findings.requirement: (`@pirate-sea-race/simulation/ruins`, `@pirate-sea-race/content/ruins`, following the existing pattern with the `@pirate-sea-race/source` condition first)
